sources.title: Askold Ivantchik: Scythians, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct academic article, 2018: fourth-century history, Ateas 339 BCE and uncertainty about extent of rule; early third-century cultural changes and disputed causes; Late Scythian communities.

sources.title: Max Planck Institute: Scythian-era urbanites did not travel far from home
sources.note: Direct institutional research report, 23 January 2020: Bilsk linked settlements, ovens, foundries, granaries, millet/wheat/barley. Earlier wider Scythian-era context; no universal nomad or acreage claim.

sources.title: Ventresca Miller and colleagues: Re-evaluating Scythian lifeways
sources.note: Direct primary PLOS ONE 2021 article: archaeological context, results and discussion; wider 700 to 200 BCE sample. Medvin 15 sampled teeth, not 15 people; Mamai Gora 21 of 25 teeth within local strontium range. Bilsk sample circa 700 to 400 BCE.

sources.title: Hrechko and Peliashenko: Handmade pottery from Bilsk rampart excavations
sources.note: Direct 2022 abstract: Tsaryna Mohyla 2016 to 2017 excavations, layers late seventh to first third fifth century BCE; earlier cookingware, bowls, ladles, storage jars and later jugs/mugs.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: dress ornament in the form of a griffin
sources.note: Direct collection catalogue, 24.97.50: circa fifth century BCE, 2.7 cm high, attachment loop. Reported Maikop origin is not a secure excavated provenance.

sources.title: National Museum of the History of Ukraine: Golden pectoral
sources.note: Direct Ukrainian museum exhibition: fourth century BCE, 1149 grams, 30.6 cm diameter; Mozolevskyi discovery 21 June 1971 in Tovsta Mohyla entrance corridor near Pokrov.

sources.title: National Museum of the History of Ukraine: The gold pectoral of the Scythian ruler
sources.note: Direct museum-authored exhibit, text Yuriy Polidovych: four hollow rods, 48 figurines, lost-wax casting/soldering; top register boy milking sheep and nursing foal. Interpretations of central figures contested.

sources.title: Dimitar Draganov: The coinage of the Scythian kings in the West Pontic area
sources.note: Direct journal PDF: printed p29 introduction and next PDF page, catalogue Ateas 1 to 2. Original Greek legend ΑΤΑΙΑΣ; Heracles obverse and mounted archer reverse. Greek text verified in edition extraction, not independent facsimile inspection.

sources.title: Istvánovits and Kulcsár: Sarmatians after the Sarmatian period
sources.note: Indexed original RGZM monograph chapter, printed p399 opening: Alanic alliance disintegrated after Huns; differing regional histories including Caucasus. Direct host returns Anubis access denial; reproducible query Sarmatians forgotten people tribes retrieves original chapter.

sources.title: Glebov and Dedyulkin: First appearance of early Sarmatians in the Lower Don
sources.note: Direct DOAJ reproduction of primary journal abstract, 2020, DOI 10.15688/nav.jvolsu.2020.2.5. Rhodian stamped amphora, black-glazed kantharoi and Megarian bowls support second/third quarters second century BCE; chronological disagreement explicit. Original journal read-online link errors.

sources.title: Vyacheslav Glebov: Mirrors of the early Sarmatian culture of the Lower Don
sources.note: Direct original 2019 abstract, pp86 to104: second/first centuries BCE, two predominant types, cases/stand, about20percent whole, ritual damage hypothesis.

sources.title: Pererva and Chistobaeva: Children and young adults from early Sarmatian burials
sources.note: Direct 2018 primary paper pp32 to45. Methods pp33 to34: 58 immature individuals dated400 to100BCE; findings p35 tooth decay in one teenager and calculus on milk teeth. Avoid broad diet, famine, parasite and scurvy claims inferred from nonspecific skeletal signs.

sources.title: S. I. Kaposhina: A Sarmatian royal burial at Novocherkassk
sources.note: Direct publisher extract of 1963 excavation report, pp256 to258; Sadovy1962, planks/reeds, soot-covered cauldrons, bowls stacked upside-down under louterion. Date supplied separately from Farkas1973; do not confuse Sadovy with Khokhlach.

sources.title: Ann Farkas: Sarmatian roundels and Sarmatian art
sources.note: Direct1973 scholarly PDF pp79 to80 Sadovy phalerae hammered silver/gold leaf and beast motifs; fig4 first century BCE; text variously early/end first century so retain broad century. General ethnic attribution/provenance of acquired Met roundel not borrowed.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Reproduction of a Sarmatian collar
sources.note: Full indexed original catalogue recovered with query title plus Novocherkassk; direct rendering omits curatorial text. Modern nineteenth-century electrotype83.18.249 after first-century CE Hermitage original, Khokhlach1864; three rings/turquoise/lions.

sources.title: Pető and colleagues: Subsistence strategies of Sarmatians in the fourth and fifth centuries CE
sources.note: Indexed original 2024 primary paper. Abstract/introduction: Iranian-speaking equestrian peoples from Pontic-Caspian steppe, settled villages in Hungarian Plain; Rákóczifalva-Bagi-földek archaeobotany/zoology; cereals,cattle; twelve grape pips from four pits. Direct fulltext fetch fails; targeted indexed title+Rákóczifalva+grape reproduces results. Wider village occupied fourth to sixth, analysis fourth to fifth.

sources.title: Roman Inscriptions of Britain 583: Ribchester dedication
sources.note: Direct scholarly edition: pedestal shaft, not altar; DEO SAN first diplomatic line; expanded Deo san(cto); translation To the holy god. Internal date31August241CE. Aelius Antoninus fromMelitene and cavalry unit atBremetennacum. No claim this is native Sarmatian language or all soldiers new steppe migrants.

batchIdentityNotes.assessment: Imported 400 to 323 BCE polygon bbox 27.29727,47.25520 to 63.67924,53.59109. Overshoots Pontic Scythia eastward and omits Crimea/lower southern zone; public overview explicitly warns. No alias to scythians-bc200 or Asian Scythian labels. Bilsk and fifth-century griffin explicitly earlier. No claim that Ateas ruled all Scythia. Writing is Greek-letter personal name, not native Scythian text.

Imported100 to1BCE bbox27.58528,40.24053 to50.46710,50.33812. Broad Pontic/Caspian label, not unified polity. No alias to Alans/Sauromatians. First-centuryBCE Sadovy distinct from first-centuryCE Khokhlach. LowerVolga child study400 to100BCE clearly earlier. Hungary fourth/fifthCE and Ribchester241CE clearly later and outside map. Greek/Roman external texts not represented as native Sarmatian writing. No invented midpoint years.
